answers.question: What do we own, what do we control, and how much of the EBITDA is ours?
answers.answer: All 11 entities are consolidated in full: ₹681.84B group EBITDA (Jan 2024–Jul 2026, after eliminations, the CFO Cockpit figure). 9 entities are 100% ours. The two JVs, GE Healthcare (49%) and Kawasaki Precision Machinery (51%), are also consolidated in full in this set-up, so Wipro’s share at stake is ₹628.76B.

steps.text: Start at the group and follow OWNS and HAS_ENTITY to all 11 legal entities (ONTO_WALK).
9 entities are owned 100% with rule FULL: ₹576.25B EBITDA.
CO:4 GE Healthcare: BUS:JV OWNS it at 49%, method FULL. ₹67.79B EBITDA is consolidated, ₹33.22B at Wipro’s stake.
CO:5 Kawasaki Precision Machinery: owned 51%, method FULL. ₹37.81B consolidated, ₹19.28B at Wipro’s stake.
Entity EBITDA adds to ₹681.86B before eliminations (Executive Overview). After intercompany eliminations it is ₹681.84B, the CFO Cockpit tile.

answers.question: What is our effective stake in each JV, and what are 10 more points of Kawasaki worth?
answers.answer: GE Healthcare is 49% and Kawasaki Precision Machinery 51%, each through the Joint Ventures business. Ten more points of Kawasaki add ₹3.78B to Wipro’s share of EBITDA (10% of its ₹37.81B, Jan 2024–Jul 2026).

steps.text: Effective stake = the product of the stakes along the path (ONTO_WALK multiplies OWNS × HAS_ENTITY).
BUS:JV OWNS CO:5 at 51% and CO:4 at 49%.
CO:5 HAS_ENTITY ENT:TALLY-WKPM at 100%, so the effective stake is 51%.
What-if: each extra point of stake moves 1% of the entity’s ₹37.81B EBITDA to Wipro: ₹3.78B for 10 points.

answers.question: Which entities trade with each other, and what does consolidation remove?
answers.answer: Wipro Infrastructure Engineering - India (WIN1) sells to Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery (WKPM) (292 documents, 290 matched) and Wipro Infrastructure Engineering - India (WIN1) sells to Wipro Consumer Care India - South (310) (296 documents, 294 matched). Both pairs sit inside the group, so ₹9.59B of revenue is eliminated (Jan 2024–Jul 2026), as on the CFO Cockpit and Close & Consolidation.

steps.text: SELLS_TO links come from the intercompany matching: seller revenue against buyer cost per document.
Wipro Infrastructure Engineering - India (WIN1) → Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery (WKPM): 292 documents, 2 exceptions, ₹4.49B booked by the seller.
Wipro Infrastructure Engineering - India (WIN1) → Wipro Consumer Care India - South (310): 296 documents, 2 exceptions, ₹5.10B booked by the seller.
Rule on the relation: a pair is eliminated only when both sides are in scope. For the whole group both are, so the Cockpit total is after eliminations.

answers.question: Is EBITDA defined the same way in every company and every ERP?
answers.answer: Yes. There is one formula (Revenue - cost of sales - operating expenses), owned by the Group CFO. It uses 4 group accounts, and 175 local accounts in 5 ERPs map to them, with none left unmapped.

props.sample: Sales - Hydraulic Pumps, Sales - Motors & Valves
Purchase - Imported Components, Purchase - Local Components
Advertisement, Freight Inward, Office & Admin Expenses, Wages & Salaries

steps.text: KPI:EBITDA has one definition in KPI_DEFINITION: Revenue - cost of sales - operating expenses. The semantic view metric is PNL.EBITDA_INR.
USES_ACCOUNT G4000 Revenue from operations as add. MAPPED_FROM SAP S/4HANA (A) (10), Dynamics 365 (2), Tally Prime (2), SAP S/4HANA (B) (4), Oracle EBS (1).
USES_ACCOUNT G5000 Cost of sales as subtract. MAPPED_FROM SAP S/4HANA (A) (34), Oracle EBS (1), SAP S/4HANA (B) (27), Dynamics 365 (1), Tally Prime (2).
USES_ACCOUNT G5100 Intercompany purchases as subtract. MAPPED_FROM Oracle EBS (1), Tally Prime (1).
USES_ACCOUNT G6000 Operating expenses as subtract. MAPPED_FROM Tally Prime (4), Oracle EBS (4), SAP S/4HANA (A) (42), Dynamics 365 (4), SAP S/4HANA (B) (35).
Every company is measured on these same accounts, whatever ERP it books in. That is why EBITDA on the CFO Cockpit, in the agent and in the thesis tracker is the same number.

answers.ask: Which accounts in which ERP make up EBITDA?

answers.question: How fast can a newly acquired company report on our definitions?
answers.answer: As soon as its ledger is mapped. Kawasaki Precision Machinery books in Tally Prime with ledger names, not account numbers, and its 9 Tally ledgers already land on the same EBITDA accounts as SAP (G6000: 4, G5100: 1, G4000: 2, G5000: 2). The next acquisition adds mapping rules for its ledger. No KPI changes.

props.sample: Advertisement, Freight Inward, Office & Admin Expenses, Wages & Salaries
Sales - Hydraulic Pumps, Sales - Motors & Valves
Purchase - Imported Components, Purchase - Local Components

steps.text: Kawasaki Precision Machinery RECORDS_IN ERP:TALLY, a different ledger with its own ledger names.

Mapping rules connect the Tally ledgers to the group accounts (MAPPED_FROM): G6000 Operating expenses ← Advertisement, Freight Inward, Office & Admin Expenses, Wages & Salaries; G5100 Intercompany purchases ← Purchase - Group Components (WIN); G4000 Revenue from operations ← Sales - Hydraulic Pumps, Sales - Motors & Valves; G5000 Cost of sales ← Purchase - Imported Components, Purchase - Local Components.
KPI:EBITDA uses those group accounts, so Kawasaki is measured on the same definition as company 1 on SAP.

answers.question: When the board asks for “debtor days”, what exactly does the agent compute?
answers.answer: “Debtor days” is a governed synonym of KPI:DSO = Trade receivables / trailing 3-month revenue x 91. That means G1200 Trade receivables (numerator) and G4000 Revenue from operations (denominator), read from 38 local accounts. Example: Consumer Care International is at 207 days as of 2026-07, as on Working Capital & Cash. The agent passed 20/21 test questions in its last evaluation.

props.sample: Sales - Hydraulic Pumps, Sales - Motors & Valves

steps.text: CONCEPT_SYNONYM resolves “debtor days”, “collection period” and Tally’s “Sundry Debtors” to KPI:DSO. The semantic view metric is WC.DSO_DAYS.
USES_ACCOUNT G1200 Trade receivables as numerator. MAPPED_FROM SAP S/4HANA (A), SAP S/4HANA (B), Tally Prime, Dynamics 365, Oracle EBS.
USES_ACCOUNT G4000 Revenue from operations as denominator. MAPPED_FROM SAP S/4HANA (A), Dynamics 365, Tally Prime, SAP S/4HANA (B), Oracle EBS.
The agent selects this metric instead of writing its own formula. The evaluation set checks its answers against the screen.

Off track: Wipro Consumer Care International cash (207 days against 90 days); Wipro Infrastructure Engineering cash (103 days against 90 days); Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery growth (8.4% against 12.0%). 5 more levers are at risk, within tolerance.

Each lever TRACKS_KPI a governed KPI. Its actual comes from V_ONTO_KPI_ACTUAL, the CFO Cockpit figure for that company and FY2026.

Wipro Infrastructure Engineering · Cash: 103 days (as of 2026-07) against a target of 90 days, off track.
Wipro Infrastructure Engineering · Growth: 9.9% (YTD Jan-Jul 2026 vs 2025) against a target of 12.0%, at risk.

Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery · Growth: 8.4% (YTD Jan-Jul 2026 vs 2025) against a target of 12.0%, off track.

answers.question: Which thesis misses will show up in cash and in the forecast?
answers.answer: Cash (DSO): Wipro Consumer Care International 207 days against 90 days; Wipro Infrastructure Engineering 103 days against 90 days; Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery 63 days against 60 days. Growth: Wipro Infrastructure Engineering 9.9% against 12.0%; Wipro Consumer Care India 8.0% against 10.0%; Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery 8.4% against 12.0%.

steps.text: Cash levers TRACKS_KPI KPI:DSO, the same DSO as Working Capital & Cash, at each company’s as-of month.
Growth levers TRACKS_KPI KPI:REVENUE_GROWTH, the same year-to-date growth as the CFO Cockpit tile for that company.
So each miss opens on the page that explains it: Working Capital & Cash for DSO, Forecast & Scenarios for growth.

answers.question: How is a thesis lever measured, and can it drift from the P&L definition?
answers.answer: It can’t drift, because the lever has no formula of its own. Kawasaki’s growth lever TRACKS_KPI KPI:REVENUE_GROWTH, which uses GA:G4000, which is MAPPED_FROM 2 Tally ledgers (Sales - Hydraulic Pumps, Sales - Motors & Valves). Actual 8.4% against a target of 12.0%.

props.sample: Sales - Hydraulic Pumps, Sales - Motors & Valves

steps.text: DEAL:05 ACQUIRED_AS CO:5 Kawasaki Precision Machinery, and HAS_LEVER LEV:05:GROWTH with a 12.0% target.
The lever TRACKS_KPI KPI:REVENUE_GROWTH. Its actual, 8.4% YTD Jan-Jul 2026 vs 2025, is the CFO Cockpit growth tile for company 5.
The KPI USES_ACCOUNT GA:G4000 revenue, which is MAPPED_FROM Kawasaki’s Tally sales ledgers.
Deal, company, entity, ledger and KPI form one connected path: change the definition once and the Cockpit, the agent and the thesis tracker all follow.
